## What was asked for

add a flag

## Where to look

This workspace has already been worked in by: review.
Their work is on disk, and against `abc123` you can see exactly what changed:

```
git diff abc123
git status
```

Judge what is there. You have not been given their reasoning, on purpose — read the change,
not an account of it.

## Merge main

A person asked for this (`nemia merge`): the work no longer merges cleanly onto `main`, which moved since. Merge it in,
at the commit their trial merge read:

    git merge def4567890

- In each conflict, keep both meanings: what this change does, and what `main` changed. Where both cannot hold, sign off
  blocked and name the choice in `needs`.
- Run the check (`npm test && npm run typecheck && npm run lint`), and fix what the merge broke — nothing else. Commit the merge.
- This is no review round: there are no findings to answer, and your `replies` are an empty list.

When you have signed off, review runs again and reads the merge. The round stays as it is.

## Before you sign off

This must exit 0 in this workspace: `npm test && npm run typecheck && npm run lint`

The run executes it afterwards, where the work is, and nothing that waits on this step starts
until it does. Do not weaken it to pass it: the command comes from the run, not from this checkout.

## Files for the steps after you

A screenshot, a log or a report reaches the steps after you and the person who decides in either of two ways.

- Put it in `/art/implement`, and name it in `artifacts` by absolute path. The run made that directory for
  this step, outside every workspace, so a file there does not ride the branch.
- Or leave it in this workspace, and name it in `artifacts` by its path from the workspace root, such as
  `RESPONSE.md` or `.e2e/shot.png`. When you finish, the run copies each such file into that directory, at the
  same path, before it checks your work, so a step that cannot write outside its workspace hands its files over
  all the same. A file left in the workspace is committed with the rest too, unless git ignores it.

The run's check of this step is given the same directory as `WF_ARTIFACTS`. Refused, and not read: an absolute
path anywhere else, and a path that climbs out of the workspace with `..`. A directory is not collected, nor a
file that is not there: name each file.

A closeout that names a file the run does not then have is refused: nothing that waits on you starts, and you are asked again, told each such name.

A file whose path passes through `.claude`, a folder a harness reads as its own configuration, is
refused, and not handed over: the steps after you read your files in a folder of theirs, and would take it as their own.

## When you are finished

Your final answer is a structured closeout, and it is how this run knows you are done. The session
asks you for it in the required shape when you finish — in Claude Code, by calling the
`StructuredOutput` tool. There is no file to write.

- `outcome`: `"done"` if you finished the work; `"blocked"` if you cannot honestly finish. A step
  that reports success it did not have is worse than one that stops and says why.
- `apiVersion`: `"nemia/v1"`.
- `summary`: one line of at most 120 characters on what you did, for the person who decides what ships. A longer
  one is cut, and the whole of it leads the body.
- `body`: markdown, everything the summary has no room for; `null` when there is nothing more.
- `artifacts`: files you wrote for someone else to read, each `{"path"}`, such as `RESPONSE.md`. Leave them in this
  workspace: when you finish, the run commits whatever you left, so the next step receives it.
  Commit your own work if you can. If you cannot — some sandboxes keep git read-only — that is
  **not** a reason to block. A file you list that the run does not then have refuses this closeout:
  you are asked again, told which.
  An artifact may be a value instead, `{"name", "value"}`, such as a pull request's address: shown labelled, and as a link
  when it is an http(s) address. `closeout.json` is the run's own name: an artifact that names it is refused.
- `needs`: only when blocked, what a person has to settle; `null` when done. A `done` closeout with a `needs` is refused.
- `replies`: `[]`. You were handed no findings this round. If a later round hands you some, you answer each there.

**Give it once, and give it last**, after everything else. The run reads it as your final word
and may start the next step on it.
